chunks: From him, from Al-Fadl and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man entered with a group in their prayer, while he did not intend it to be a prayer. Then their Imam broke his ablution, so he took the hand of that man and brought him forward, so he led them in prayer. Would their prayer be sufficient by his prayer, while he did not intend it to be a prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: It is not befitting for the man that he enters with a group in their prayer while he does not intend it to be a prayer, but it is befitting for him that he intends it to be a prayer. If he had already prayed, then he has another prayer, otherwise he should not enter with them. Their prayer would suffice for the group, even if he did not intend it.
Their prayer would suffice for the group, even if he did not intend it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man joining a prayer without intending it as a prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of joining a congregational prayer (Salat al-Jama'ah) without prior specific intention, ruling that the Imam (peace be upon him) validates the congregation's prayer even if the latecomer does not intend it as a distinct obligatory act. It establishes that if the individual has already fulfilled their duty, the late entry serves as supererogatory (Nafl), whereas if not, they must intend it to be valid. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the flexibility of niyyah in communal settings, prioritizing the unity of the congregation over rigid individual intentionality for the latecomer.

en.hubeali: From him, from Al Fazl, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘A man enters with a group into their Salāt and he does not intend it to be a Salāt. So their Imam breaks his ablution, and he grabs the hand of that man and moves him forward for him so lead Salāt with them. Would their Salāts be sufficed by his Salāt and he did not intend it to be in a Salāt?’ So heasws said: ‘It is not befitting for the man that he enters with a group into their Salāt and he does not intend it to be in a Salāt, but, it is befitting for him that he intends it as a Salāt. Then, if it was so that he had already prayed Salāt, so it would be another Salāt for him, or else, so he should not enter with them. It would have sufficed from the group, their Salāt, and even if he did not intend it as so’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by al-Fadl and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who comes to a people during their Salah (prayer) and he is not intending it to be Salah (prayer). Their Imam faces invalidation of his Wudu’ and holds the hand of this man and makes him to lead. He performs Salah (prayer) with them. Is his Salah (prayer) sufficient to complete their Salah (prayer) while he has not intended it to be Salah (prayer)? He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not proper for a man to come to a people in their Salah (prayer) and not intend it to be Salah (prayer). It is proper for him to intend it to be Salah (prayer). If he has already performed Salah (prayer) he has another Salah (prayer). Otherwise, he must not come to them;
their Salah (prayer) is sufficient for them even if he did not intend it to be Salah (prayer).”’
